lyrics:
[Intro: shrieking high string stabs, twangy surf guitar, fast beat]

[Verse 1: breathy, close, half whispered]
Doctor, doctor, I've been reading all the signs
Hives on my good sense, itching in my mind
Every time you call me I come up in a rash
Every time I answer I'm a little more attached

[Pre-Chorus: bass drops out, voice rises]
I should stay away
Far, far away
But I keep leaning in

[Chorus: high falsetto, strings shriek between lines]
I'm allergic to you
Breaking out and I can't stop
One more look and my heart goes pop
Allergic, allergic
And I keep coming back for more
Somebody tell me what the pills are for

[Verse 2: breathy, playful, surf guitar answers]
Read the label, read it twice, it said avoid
My friends all say there's something for it, I say I'm paranoid
Got a fever, got a flutter, got a tingle in my hands
Got an appointment Thursday and a whole lot of other plans

[Pre-Chorus: bass drops out, voice rises]
I should stay away
Far, far away
But I keep leaning in

[Chorus: high falsetto, strings shriek between lines]
I'm allergic to you
Breaking out and I can't stop
One more look and my heart goes pop
Allergic, allergic
And I keep coming back for more
Somebody tell me what the pills are for

[Bridge: beat halves, wordless falsetto, strings slide down]
Ah, ah-ah, ah
I'm old enough to know
Ah, ah-ah, ah
And I still go

[Breakdown: surf guitar solo, handclaps]

[Final Chorus: everything, extra string line, ad-libs]
I'm allergic to you
Breaking out and I can't stop
One more look and my heart goes pop
Allergic, allergic
And I keep coming back for more
Somebody tell me what the pills are for
I'm allergic to you

[Outro: string stab, a sneeze, a giggle]
producerBrief:
TEMPO / KEY / FEEL: 143 BPM, 4/4, C minor. Fast, tense and slinky. A spy-film chase on a dance floor.

VOICE: Female, breathy and close, nearly whispered in the verses with a little nasal edge. The chorus is sung in a thin, bright falsetto, layered several times. Wordless falsetto 'ah's in the bridge. Playful, not tragic.

INSTRUMENTS: High orchestral strings playing short, shrieking, sliding stabs, the song's signature. A twangy, reverb-heavy surf electric guitar. A fast, tight electronic drum pattern. A driving synth bass. Acoustic guitar strums buried in the chorus. Handclaps.

ARRANGEMENT MAP: 0:00 Intro, string stabs and surf guitar. 0:10 Verse 1. 0:27 Pre-chorus, the bass drops out. 0:37 Chorus 1. 0:57 Verse 2. 1:14 Pre-chorus. 1:24 Chorus 2. 1:44 Bridge, the beat halves. 2:04 Breakdown, a short surf-guitar solo over claps. 2:17 Final chorus with an extra string line. 2:50 The hook repeats with ad-libs. 3:05 Outro, one last string stab, a sneeze and a giggle at 3:15.

PRODUCTION & MIX: Early-2000s Swedish electro-pop: bright, tight and dense, strings and guitar hard left and right, vocal breathy and very close.

SIGNATURE MOMENT: The string stabs in the first two seconds.

MODERN POINT OF VIEW: The bridge is the difference: 'I'm old enough to know, and I still go.' It is the same temptation with twenty more years of evidence, played for a smile.

EMOTIONAL ARC: Mock alarm, giving in, self-knowledge, giving in again.
